sanskrit: indrasya bāhū sthavirau vṛṣāṇau citrā imā vṛṣabhau pārayiṣṇū | tau yokṣye prathamau yoga āgate yābhyāṃ jitam asurāṇāṃ svar yat ||
english: Indra's two arms — sturdy, bull-powerful, these two wondrous bulls that carry across — I shall yoke them first when the time of yoking arrives, those two by which the heavenly light of the asuras was won.

sanskrit: āśuḥ śiśāno vṛṣabho na bhīmo ghanāghanaḥ kṣobhaṇaś carṣaṇīnām | saṃkrandano 'nimiṣa ekavīraḥ śataṃ senā jayatu sākam indraḥ ||
english: Swift, being whetted, terrible as a bull, crusher of crushers, shaker of the peoples — the Saṃkrandana, unwinking, sole hero: may Indra conquer a hundred armies together.

sanskrit: saṃkrandanenānimiṣeṇa jiṣṇunā- -ayodhyena duścyavanena dhṛṣṇunā | tad indreṇa jayata tat sahadhvaṃ yudho nara iṣuhastena vṛṣṇā ||
english: With the Saṃkrandana, with the unwinking, with the victorious, with the irresistible, with the hard-to-dislodge, with the bold — conquer through Indra; hold firm together, O men of battle, through the rain-bull who holds the arrow in hand.

sanskrit: sa iṣuhastaiḥ sa niṣaṅgibhir vaśī saṃsraṣṭā yudha indro gaṇena | saṃsṛṣṭajit somapā bāhuśardhy ūrdhvadhanvā pratihitābhir astāt ||
english: He, the subduer, with arrow-wielders, with quiver-bearers, Indra who enters battle joined with his troop — victor in close combat, soma-drinker, bold-armed, bow-upraised: may he shoot with fitted arrows.

sanskrit: balavijñāyaḥ sthaviraḥ pravīraḥ sahasvān vājī sahamāna ugraḥ | abhivīro abhiṣatvā sahojij jaitrāyendra ratham ā tiṣṭha govidam ||
english: Distinguished by strength, ancient, foremost warrior, enduring, prize-winning, bearing-down, fierce — hero-against-hero, who overwhelms fighters, victor through might — mount the chariot for conquest, O Indra, the cow-finder.

sanskrit: imaṃ vīram anu harṣadhvam ugram indraṃ satvāno anu saṃ rabhadhvam | grāmajitaṃ gojitaṃ vajrabāhuṃ jayantam ajma pramṛṇantam ojasā ||
english: Exult after this fierce hero; O battle-men, rally together after Indra — the village-conquerer, cattle-conquerer, bolt-armed, conquering in his onrush, crushing with might.

sanskrit: abhi gotrāṇi sahasā gāhamāno adāya ugraḥ śatamanyur indraḥ | duścyavanaḥ pṛtanāṣāḍ ayodhyo asmākaṃ senā avatu pra yutsu ||
english: Plunging into the cattle-herds with force, taking them away unstopped, the fierce, hundred-thoughted Indra — hard to dislodge, battle-overwhelming, irresistible — may he protect our army, driving them forward in combat.

sanskrit: bṛhaspate pari dīyā rathena rakṣohāmitrām̐ apabādhamānaḥ | prabhañjañ chatrūn pramṛṇann amitrān asmākam edhy avitā tanūnām ||
english: O Bṛhaspati, wheel around with your chariot, repelling demons and foes — breaking enemies, crushing adversaries: be our protector of bodies.

sanskrit: indra āsāṃ netā bṛhaspatir dakṣiṇā yajñaḥ pura etu somaḥ | devasenānām abhibhañjatīnāṃ jayantīnāṃ maruto yantu madhye ||
english: Indra is their leader, Bṛhaspati the sacrificial fee, let the sacrifice go before, let Soma advance first — may the Maruts march in the midst of the divine armies that overwhelm, that are victorious.

sanskrit: indrasya vṛṣṇo varuṇasya rājña ādityānāṃ marutāṃ śardha ugram | mahāmanasāṃ bhuvanacyavānāṃ ghoṣo devānāṃ jayatām ud asthāt ||
english: Of Indra the bull, of Varuṇa the king, of the Ādityans, of the fierce host of the Maruts — of the great-minded, the world-shaking — the battle-roar of the gods has risen to victory.

sanskrit: asmākam indraḥ samṛteṣu dhvajeṣv asmākaṃ yā iṣavas tā jayantu | asmākaṃ vīrā uttare bhavantv asmān devāso 'vatā haveṣu ||
english: Indra is ours at the clashing of banners; may our arrows be victorious; may our heroes be uppermost; may the gods protect us at our callings.

sanskrit: vaiśvānarād arocata jāto hiraṇyayo maṇiḥ | tam ābharad bṛhaspatiḥ kaśyapo vīryāya kam ||
english: From Vaiśvānara there shone forth, newborn, the golden amulet. Bṛhaspati brought it, Kaśyapa brought it, for power indeed.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatis tam akṛṇon maṇiṃ vaiśvānaraṃ sahaḥ | saptarṣayo balāya kaṃ saṃ dadhuṣ ṭvā vayodhasaḥ ||
english: Bṛhaspati fashioned that amulet as Vaiśvānara's might. The Seven Seers, increasers of life, have bestowed you for strength.

sanskrit: viśve devās ta indriyaṃ saptarṣayaś ca saṃ dadhuḥ | jāto hiraṇyayo maṇir agner vaiśvānarād adhi ||
english: All the gods and the Seven Seers have together bestowed your virile power. You were born as a golden amulet from Agni Vaiśvānara.

sanskrit: aśvattho jātaḥ prathamo 'gneḥ priyatamā tanūḥ | vaiśvānarasya sṛṣṭyā kṛtyādūṣiḥ kṛto maṇiḥ ||
english: The aśvattha tree was born first, the dearest body of Agni — by the creative power of Vaiśvānara this amulet was made the neutralizer of kṛtyā.

sanskrit: kṛtyādūṣiṃ tvāvidaṃ kṛtyādūṣiṃ bharāmi tvā | kṛtyādūṣiṃ kṛṇomi tvā kṛtyādūṣiṃ vayodhasam ||
english: I know you as kṛtyā-neutralizer; I carry you as kṛtyā-neutralizer; I make you the kṛtyā-neutralizer, the kṛtyā-neutralizer that sustains life.

sanskrit: patatrī pakṣī balavān kṛtyādūṣiḥ sapatnahā | nitatnir viśvabheṣaja ugra āpatiko maṇiḥ ||
english: The winged one, the feathered, the powerful kṛtyā-neutralizer, the rival-slayer — the broadly extended, all-healing, fierce, suddenly-striking amulet.

sanskrit: patatrī te balāya kaṃ nitatnir bheṣajāya te | jāto hiraṇyayo maṇir apa rakṣāṃsi sedhatu ||
english: The winged one is for your strength; the broadly extended one for your healing. May the golden amulet, newborn, drive away the demons.

sanskrit: devo maṇiḥ sapatnahā rakṣohāmīvacātanaḥ | hiraṇyayonir aṃśumān kaśyapenābhṛtaṃ sahaḥ ||
english: The divine amulet, rival-slayer, demon-killer, disease-chaser — of golden womb, full of rays: the might brought by Kaśyapa.

sanskrit: vaiśvānaraṃ tejanam ekam āhur agner yoneḥ saha candreṇa jātam | gayasphānaḥ prataraṇo vayodhāḥ kṛtyādūṣir valagahāsy ugraḥ ||
english: They call the Vaiśvānara one a sharpener, born from the womb of Agni together with the Moon — the prosperer of households, the one that carries across, the sustainer of life; you are a fierce kṛtyā-neutralizer, you who smash the valagaha.

sanskrit: yasyedaṃ bhūmyām adhi nikrāntaṃ pāṃsure padam | mṛjānas tanvo yad rapas tasya snāhi tanū adhi ||
english: Whoever's footprint is impressed upon this dusty earth — cleansing away whatever bodily taint is his, bathe upon his body.

sanskrit: dūṣyās tvā vadhaṃ vayaṃ devasya savituḥ save | jīvātave bharāmasi mahyā ariṣṭatātaye ||
english: We, deserving of the smiting, carry you at the impulsion of divine Savitṛ — for living, for our great unharmed state.

sanskrit: ācchedanaḥ pracchedano dviṣatas tapano maṇiḥ | śatruñjayaḥ sapatnahā dviṣantam apa bādhatām ||
english: The cutting-through, the piercing-through, the scorcher of the enemy — this amulet: the enemy-conquering rival-slayer. May it drive away the one who hates.

sanskrit: satyasya sthūṇā pṛthivīṃ dādhāra ṛtena devā amṛtam anv avindan | dhruveṇa tvā haviṣā dhārayāmy abhi tad dyāvāpṛthivī gṛṇītām ||
english: The pillar of truth upheld the earth; through cosmic order the gods found immortality. With the firm oblation I uphold you — may Heaven and Earth acclaim that.

sanskrit: yebhir homair viśvakarmā dādhāremāṃ pṛthivīṃ mātaraṃ naḥ | tebhiṣ ṭvā homair iha dhārayāmy ṛtaṃ satyam anu carantu homāḥ ||
english: With those oblations by which Viśvakarman upheld this earth, our mother — with those oblations I uphold you here. May the oblations follow upon cosmic order and truth.

sanskrit: iha dhriyadhvaṃ dharuṇe pṛthivyā uśatyā mātuḥ subhagāyā upasthe | aparāṇuttā mahasā modamānā asmin vāstau suprajaso bhavātha ||
english: Be established here on the foundation of earth, in the lap of the willing, auspicious mother — undriven-away, rejoicing in greatness: in this dwelling may you be blessed with good offspring.

sanskrit: suprajaso mahasā modamānā varṣman pṛthivyā upari śrayadhvam | asyai śālāyai śarma yacchantu devā dhārābhir enāṃ pṛthivī pipartu ||
english: Blessed with good offspring, rejoicing in greatness, rest above on the summit of the earth. May the gods grant shelter to this house; may the earth fill it with streams.

sanskrit: imāṃ śālāṃ śreṣṭhatamāṃ vasūnām ariṣṭavīrā abhi saṃ carema | dṛḍhā asyā upamito bhavantu sthirā vīrā upasado bhavantu ||
english: May we, with unharmed heroes, approach together this house, the best of good things. May her roof-posts be firm; may the house-dwellers be steadfast and heroic.

sanskrit: imāṃ śālāṃ savitā vāyur indro bṛhaspatir ni minotu prajānan | ukṣantūdnā maruto ghṛtena bhago no rājā ni kṛṣiṃ dadhātu ||
english: May Savitṛ, Vāyu, Indra, Bṛhaspati wisely establish this house. May the Maruts sprinkle it with water and ghee; may Bhaga our king establish prosperity.

sanskrit: mānasya patni haviṣo juṣasva tīvrāntasya bahulamadhyamasya | ā tvā śiśur vāśyatām ā kumāra ā vāśyantāṃ dhenavo nityavatsāḥ ||
english: O wife of the house-master, take pleasure in the oblation, of him whose end is keen and whose middle is copious. May a young child cry out to you, may a boy cry out, may the milk-cows with their perpetual calves cry out.

sanskrit: dṛḍhās te sthūṇā bhavantu bhūmyām adhi dṛḍhāḥ pakṣāsas tava devi śāle | sthiravīrānamitrā na edhi śarma no yaccha dvipade catuṣpade ||
english: May your posts be firm, firmly planted in the earth; may your roof-beams be firm, O divine house. Be one with steadfast heroes and no enemies; grant us shelter for two-footed and four-footed.

sanskrit: śālā devī gārhapatyāya cākl̥pe tṛṇaṃ vasānā jagate suśevā | sthirāṅgāṃ tvā sthirapūruṣāṃ mānasya patni sthirāṃ tvā vīrā abhi saṃ carema ||
english: The divine house is fitted for the householder's fire; clothed in grass, well-pleasing to the world. O wife of the house-master, may the heroes approach you with steadfast limbs, steadfast people, and steadfast dwelling.

sanskrit: vāstoṣpate prati jānīhy asmān svāveśo anamīvo na edhi | yat tvemahe prati nas taj juṣasva catuṣpado dvipada ā veśayeha ||
english: O Lord of the Dwelling, recognize us; be one of easy entry and free from sickness. What we pray to you for — take delight in that for us; let the four-footed and two-footed settle here.
